One of the worst things about this activity is that only two teams get to give thank you speeches at the end. All of us, whether we went 0-6 or 6-0, have something to be grateful for. Debate took up the better part of 4 years of my life, for better or worse. Although the season didn’t end up going the way I wanted to, it’s not an exaggeration to say that this community has given me more than I ever could’ve imagined when my mom first signed me up for classes against my will all those years ago. With that said, I’d like to thank some of the people who made debate what it was for me:

Anybody who’s ever coached me. I’m deeply indebted to all of you, especially the team at Break Debate: Vik, Jordan, Pranav, Mike, Ariel, Gong, etc. Kush too, I guess. Vaish, Holden, Cho, thank you for introducing me to the deep end of this activity in my formative years. Shreeram, I want to be like you when I grow up. Sheff, thanks for always being a friendly face at tournaments. Obligatory Etkin shoutout.

Break teammates. You guys made what could’ve been a really awkward transition year for the program quite fun. I’m especially grateful to all of my fellow seniors (Ezra, Darina, Ethan, Elaine) for sticking around. Our juniors and sophs are some of the hardest working debaters I’ve ever met, and I have confidence that all of you will have great careers.

Vaishgang: Nettam, Phil, Nate, Ava, Arnav. I wrote a college essay about you guys. Truly the best friends I could have wished for. We should run Gartic again, it’s been too long.

Vikrant. It’s hard to express in words how glad I am that we reconnected this year. Conversations with you are some of the most fun I’ve had in this activity, while also being the hardest I’ve ever had to think. Thanks for putting up with my BS, tweak outs, and quadruple texts. I know you’ll kill it at Michigan.

Ethan. You’re one of the most impressive debaters I’ve ever met, and I’m proud to have worked together. Peninsula was super fun. Keep lighting up rooms wherever you go next.

Darina. We had so many fun debates, despite the fact that nearly none involved evaluating the desirability of a topical action (who would’ve thought). You’re one of the smartest and funniest people I’ve ever met. Columbia isn't ready.

Koov. It sounds weird to say this to a 17 year old, but I unironically look up to you. Although your takes pmo sometimes, you’re one of the smartest people I’ve ever met and I mean it when I say that I think you’re going to change the world.

Woland. I don’t always understand what you’re saying, but when I do, it’s always brilliant and hilarious. 

Om, Bo, Nilesh. It’s lynsane how talented, kind, and funny all of you are. DoLSD.

Harker. All of you were very fun to debate, despite the fact that our rounds somehow never ended up being about the plan. Mb.

Nikhil, Antonio, Vishal, Bodhi, Nickford, etc. I seriously doubt any of you are reading this right now, but if you are, thank you. Coming into debate as a freshman from Illinois was genuinely intimidating, but you all made it immeasurably easier.

ADC:
Will. Thanks for being a ray of sunshine in the dark tunnel of LD. You always offered unconditional support, even when I didn’t deserve it, and I’m forever grateful.
Nato. Your brutal honesty played a big part in shaping who I am today. We should talk sometime.
Lydia. You were a great friend and coach. Thanks for teaching me the Politics DA.
Ike. If I’d known that you would go on to win the NDT, I would’ve played a lot more Stardew Valley with you. JK. 

Judges:
Pat. Thanks for everything. Your feedback was instrumental in shaping me as a debater, and I always looked forward to having you in the back. 
Nick Loew. Thanks for sitting for me twice. You always knew The Truth, an enviable quality.
Michael Harris. Despite the fact that I never learned anything about philosophy, and you nothing about policy, you were always high on my sheet. 

Thanks to everyone from CFMP. DML, Kurt, Pipkin, Dr. Chase, it was an honor to learn from you guys. Nate, Ava, Ezra, Arjun, Kento, Jaxson, Lucy, Sophie, Jack, Paul, Maikle, Mason, etc: camp was super fun with you guys, and I learned something from all of you.

This is far from a conclusive list, and I’m sure I’ve missed tons of people who I will miss dearly. Apologies for that. 

I love all of you. I love debate. I’d do it all again in a heartbeat. Thanks for everything. 

Barrington AC, out.

Wow. William Li. What a career. 

I still remember my first sighting of William; a Peninsula prelim, my freshman year, as he fiercely battled Shiwen. He was affirmative versus the demining PIC, and boy was he a sight to see. 

I can't say it was a shock when, the following weekend, he overcame Village SZ to Champion THE Columbia University Invitational tournament.

But he didn't slow there; he steamrolled all the way to the DOUBLE-OCTAFINALS of the Berkeley Tournament, where he was felled by THE Kabir Buch in an incredibly close debate. Though William Li had that SAUCE with the Bomb Iran CP, he unfortunately didn't realize he needed to answer 'Counterforce Existential.' 

This loss was FUEL. William Li CAME BACK, Quarterfinalling not JUST DSDS2, but ALSO DSDS3. Just incredible work, all around.

This year, William Li wasn't playing around. After fighting all the way to the FINALS of the Peninsula Tournament (and OBLITERATING Nikhil in the process), William showed that he is that guy.

To cap off his phenomenal run, he FINALLED the Cal RR, and made it the Quarterfinals of the Berkeley tournament. 

Throughout it all, William battled the adversity that comes with being a small school debater, and persevered after being denied EVEN the TOC, his SENIOR year.

William is one of my best friends in the activity, and is a true SHARK in this space, refining (with Tomas Gonzales) the most fabulous positions, such as the A&S Fiat P, and the INFAMOUS Heg Bad K.

Thank you for everything, William Li.

Wow. William. Where do I begin. 

I still remember meeting William for the first time at TDI. I was straight out of my frosh year, quite intimidated by a new environment. I recognized him from the round online when he debated a senior from my school, but I was afraid to speak to him. He approached me kindly, and invited me to a game of Clash Royale. I gave a speech in front of him, and he told me I was surprisingly good. That summer, we played basketball (shoutout Elmer), league, and debated together. We hung out every night doing prep and annoying Justin. For someone who just joined debate 6 months ago, he was one of the first friends I've made on the circuit.

We both joined the ADC, where William mentored me for the rest of the summer. I remember sitting in the community room with Elmer discussing the living wage topic, and ultimately, with Lizzie's help, pushing for the selection of that topic. I also remember staying up late processing cards with you, writing my first ever K aff. You handed me blocks for the "Predictability K" and the "Set Col K," which immediately got me, a clueless novice, a bid over the bid leader from the previous season. At the time, I couldn't comprehend such strategy at all, but I know that William got me right. 

It is fair to say that William is one of the brightest minds in debate. Whether it is breaking even at the TOC as a sophomore with zero coaching, churning out the most innovative positions, or being able to do the fastest but also best delivered line-by-line I've ever seen, William got it. I truly believe that, if you were granted more opportunity, you would've been one of the most dominating forces on the circuit. 

I cried a lot in debate. I cried for losing, but I have rarely cried outside of a tournament. There was one exception: I still remember being on the drive to Kentucky just to hear that you got ill and couldn't show up for your final (junior) year of the TOC. I burst into tears, knowing you deserved it, and I really expected something great from you that weekend.

Throughout it all, William is probably one of the most influential people in my career. He taught me, a traditional public forum debater who couldn't speak much English at the time, the specifics of technical debating and a recipe for success. It was he who, in the midst of a busy junior year, had the patience for an egotistical sophomore who repeatedly rejected advice. It was he who, even when I was his competition, taught me the strategies he relied on. It is not crazy to say that William has shaped my conception of debate. Although we go for different arguments now, it was William who introduced me to arguments ranging from paraconsistent logic to the regime change counterplan, and more importantly, taught me how to give judge instructions, how to sound ethosy, and how to be creative.

English was my second language, and I was never a good writer. My words cannot express how much gratitude I owe to you, or how big of an impact you had on my career. We will forever remember "Postmemory," the "Justice Aff," "McFellin 22," "Flip Time Theory," "1NC vs King Kai," and most importantly, you as a dedicated Bayesian sloper. Great career, William. Excited to see what's next in your coaching journey.

William Li is more than just a person. He represents a promise. A promise to improve, a promise to see the best in others, and most importantly a promise to always be a kind and thoughtful person. 

The first time I met William was at the TOC my freshman year. After our round (where I spent all 6 minutes of my 2NR extending a DA without answering a single 1AR argument), William struck up a conversation with me. After discovering that I also played Clash of Clans, he was quick to add me as a friend and give me tips on how to improve my base layout. 

Fast forward a year to the Jack Howe Memorial tournament. After William and I had a super educational round, debating the merits of decolonization vs the risks of a civil war, he came back with me to the HW squad room. There, we played some hangman (which was the only time I managed to beat William at something), chatted with Meza about life, and William gave me some tips on classes I should take my junior year. 

If it isn't obvious by now, my first few interactions with William followed the same basic formula: I would get brutally destroyed by him in a debate, he and I would talk for a bit after the round, and I would always be left with a piece of advice or guidance from him that I never would have expected from someone I barely knew. 

The rest of his junior (and my sophomore) year included one debate at peninsula which I don't want to talk about, one skipped TOC, and a lot more time where we got to know each other better/talked more frequently. However, William and I only really became close over this past season. Whether I wanted someone to vent to about how terribly my physics test went, needed advice on how to improve my word economy, or had no one to eat lunch with at a tournament, William was always there for me with encouraging words, helpful tips, and great food recommendations. 

William and I have had a ton of awesome memories together and I am super sad that he is graduating this year. Although he has beaten me every time that we have debated, I was always excited when I glance at the pairing and see Bellevue/Washington Independent/Sharks Independent WL because I knew that I had an awesome round ahead of me. I know that he has great things ahead of him in the future and that I have made a friend for life who I can always rely on. 

Thank you so much William for being an amazing friend. We have both come so far sense round 3 of our first TOC and I am so grateful I met you.

"hey bro u got me too right W victor"

Boy oh boy, where do I even start with William Li? I remember back in the day, William sent me a condo file and I replied after 12 hours and said "oops i forgot to thank you thank you!" 

After that, we prepped lay cases for UKSO and William lost all of his lay rounds, which is where our friendship really started.

From going 1-3 at the University of Michigan HS Debate Tournament together to prerounding to quarters at Cal to breaking MY file new to win the Cal RR, William’s success this season, especially as an independent who wasn’t even allowed to go to the TOC his senior year, really can’t be understated. 

More than that, William has long been debate’s Robin Hood---helping me cut files, prerounding me to a 3-0 finals loss with sketchy impact turns, and running more PRs with me than everything else (which often concluded with the 2AR saying “Victor sucks at debate… uhh good round”), and certainly doing the same for others. Even if he had to scrape his volunteering hours, those don’t reflect at all the sheer magnitude of the impact William has had on shaping young debaters. 

But if William is remembered at all, I hope he won’t only be remembered as “that guy who only bids at online tournaments and was p mid.” More than anything else, throughout this entire year, William has been one of the best friends I could ask for---being nervous about my college apps, complaining about my personal life, talking about how AP Environmental Science is easy, and discussing the intricacies of the Straw Hat Grand Fleet---William’s been there through it with me all, and has helped me through it all, even with the frequent ghosting, and I'd be shocked if there weren't dozens with the same story. 

In more ways than one, William is an anchor---to me, to a large portion of the community (and the unbounded group chats he’s part of), and… 

Even though I probably wouldn’t have written this if he hadn’t asked me to, I’m grateful from the bottom of my heart to William---as someone who started LD only as a junior, and barely broke until December last year, I am genuinely unsure if I would have the one bid I did get, or if I would have stayed in the activity at all; I made some of my best memories in debate and in my senior year writ large as a direct result of him, and William is definitely in the S tier of underrated/dark horse debaters in the community. 

I hope that our friendship continues past graduation, and that we can run up an NDT/CEDA tournament---and hopefully not go 1-3.

Affirmative: Advocated a utilitarian framework, weighing impacts by consistency with utilitarianism and arguing that extinction outweighs all other harms. Claimed governments must evaluate policies by outcomes, not intentions. Advanced two advantages: climate change and pollination. Asserted that climate change is an accelerating existential risk driven by greenhouse gas emissions, with rewilding uniquely essential in the United States to sequester carbon, restore ecosystems, and prevent irreversible tipping points. Further argued that rewilding preserves pollinators, which are critical to food production, nutrition, and global food security; pollinator collapse increases mortality, destabilizes agriculture, and escalates conflict. Concluded that rewilding prevents extinction-level risks and maximizes overall good, affirming the resolution.

Negative: Advocated a framework of morality, with a criterion of utilitarianism. Argued that policy decisions should maximize overall good and prevent the greatest harm, with extinction outweighing all other impacts. Advanced an economic disadvantage claiming federal rewilding collapses confidence, crowds out investment, and triggers recession, which escalates into great-power conflict and nuclear war. Asserted that large-scale rewilding is prohibitively expensive and undermines economic growth, which is key to environmental sustainability. Offered a counterplan transferring rewilding authority to states and territories to preserve environmental benefits while avoiding federal economic collapse.

Negative: Advocated a framework of morality, with a criterion of utilitarianism, arguing that ethical policy should maximize overall good and minimize harm, with extinction outweighing all other impacts. Claimed that rewilding 30% of U.S. land is substantial and triggers an economic disadvantage: large-scale rewilding is prohibitively expensive, exacerbates Farm Bill gridlock, and requires massive government spending that collapses consumer and business confidence. Argued the economy is fragile and that a confidence shock causes recession, which escalates into great-power conflict and nuclear war. Concluded that economic growth is a prerequisite to environmental sustainability, making federal rewilding immoral under utilitarian calculus.

Negative: Advocated a framework of Mortality Reduction, with a criterion of Nuclear Deterrence. Argued that nuclear weapons prevent great-power war, reduce conventional warfare casualties, and limit the proliferation and use of chemical and biological weapons. Key contentions included the deterrence disadvantage and a weapons shift argument.

Negative: Advocated a framework of Mortality Reduction, with a criterion of Nuclear Deterrence. Argued that nuclear weapons prevent great-power war, reduce conventional warfare casualties, and limit the proliferation and use of chemical and biological weapons. Key contentions included the deterrence disadvantage and a weapons shift argument.

Negative: Advocated a framework of morality, with a criterion of minimizing structural violence. Argued that the possession of nuclear weapons is only immoral if it produces greater harm than its alternatives. Claimed that nuclear deterrence prevents invasion, great-power war, and large-scale casualties by raising the cost of aggression to unacceptable levels. Key contentions included deterrence failure producing structural violence (using Ukraine as an empirical example), nuclear weapons as the strongest security guarantee in an anarchic international system, and empirical evidence that deterrence reduces death and violence without requiring use.

rounds.tournament: Tri State Debate League at Brooklyn Tech
rounds.report: Affirmative: Advocated a value of justice with a criterion of utilitarianism, arguing that justice must be evaluated by real-world outcomes and harm reduction rather than abstract punishment. Claimed that moral systems should prioritize practicality and minimizing suffering, citing human nature and state responsibility for consequences. Advanced three contentions. First, efficiency: plea bargaining is the backbone of the U.S. criminal justice system, preventing court collapse, massive backlogs, and taxpayer waste, while allowing prosecutors to prioritize serious crimes. Second, crime prevention: plea bargaining increases the likelihood of punishment, which best deters crime, and enables cooperation and informants essential to dismantling organized crime. Third, alternatives are worse: banning plea bargaining drives it underground or forces all cases to trial, producing longer sentences, judicial overload, increased wrongful convictions, and more coercive outcomes. Concluded that plea bargaining maximizes overall good, reduces harm, and is therefore just under a utilitarian conception of justice.

rounds.tournament: Tri State Debate League at Brooklyn Tech
rounds.report: Negative: Advocated a value of justice, defined as giving each their due, with a criterion of minimizing structural violence, prioritizing equality and the reduction of systemic harm. Argued that structural violence is the most severe and pervasive form of inequality because it is invisible, normalized by institutions, and produces widespread suffering and death comparable to direct violence. Advanced a single contention of inequality, claiming plea bargaining is a primary driver of racial disparities and mass incarceration in the United States. Asserted that mass incarceration of marginalized communities entrenches structural racism, sustains wealth and opportunity gaps, and undermines upward mobility. Cited evidence that disproportionate incarceration contributes to long-term economic insecurity, unemployment, and reduced life expectancy for Black communities, concluding that plea bargaining perpetuates structural violence and is therefore unjust.

I'd just like to interject for a moment. What you're refering to as Linux, is in fact, GNU/Linux, or as I've recently taken to calling it, GNU plus Linux. Linux is not an operating system unto itself, but rather another free component of a fully functioning GNU system made useful by the GNU corelibs, shell utilities and vital system components comprising a full OS as defined by POSIX.

Many computer users run a modified version of the GNU system every day, without realizing it. Through a peculiar turn of events, the version of GNU which is widely used today is often called Linux, and many of its users are not aware that it is basically the GNU system, developed by the GNU Project.

There really is a Linux, and these people are using it, but it is just a part of the system they use. Linux is the kernel: the program in the system that allocates the machine's resources to the other programs that you run. The kernel is an essential part of an operating system, but useless by itself; it can only function in the context of a complete operating system. Linux is normally used in combination with the GNU operating system: the whole system is basically GNU with Linux added, or GNU/Linux. All the so-called Linux distributions are really distributions of GNU/Linux!

Additional information: The 1-10 thing referenced here is the concept of Blackstone's Ratio, which states that "it is better that 10 guilty go free than 1 innocent person escape".This concept emphasizes that the moral cost of convicting even a single innocent person outweighs the benefit of punishing multiple guilty ones. Under this framework, a just system must be designed to minimize wrongful convictions above all else. I negate the resolution: Resolved: The US military ought to abide by a principle of non-intervention.

Roadmap: To support my position, I will first establish a value and criterion. Then, I will present three contentions that uphold my side of the debate. My case will be organized as follows: Shrekian Ethics, Deterrence of Potential Externalities. Contention 1: Deterring External Power Vacuums, Contention 2: Preserving Economic Sovereignty, and Contention 3: Counter-Revisionism of Territorial Integrity.

To achieve clarity in today's debate, my value is Shrekian Ethics. Shrekian Ethics is defined as a Deontological framework of Organic Sovereignty which prioritizes the preservation of the inherent right of an actor to maintain a private domain. This ethics system rejects the impulse toward artificial, sterilized global order in favor of a gritty, authentic realism. It posits that an entity’s highest moral obligation is the defense of its own perimeter against the externalization of others’ ideological or political crises. This value is crucial because it prioritizes the preservation of self-contained sovereignty over the artificial perfection of a globalist, manicured peace.

To measure whether this value is upheld, I will use the criterion of Deterrence of Potential Externalities.. This criterion is derived from the Shrekian principle that "Ogremosity" (strength) is only effective when it creates an aura of deterrence. In modern strategic terms, as we saw with the 2025 National Security Strategy, a credible willingness to act is required to enforce regional doctrines. Without active deterrence, national security is inevitably compromised by external actors.

Now that I've established my framework, let's move into my contentions.

Contentions: Contention 1: Deterring Regional Power Vacuums

Claim: Absolute non-intervention creates vacuums that invite external instability into the domestic sphere.

Warrant: When a superpower adopts a policy of total restraint, it signals to aggressive regional actors that they may externalize their political crises without consequence. This leads to the displacement of populations, the spread of extremist factions, and the spillover of conflict across sovereign borders.

Data: According to the 2025 National Security Strategy, a lack of US engagement in volatile regions directly correlates with the rise of adversarial influence and the destabilization of border security.

Impact: A failure to proactively enforce a "Get out of my swamp" policy means the state loses control over its environment, eventually finding its private domain overrun by the "fairytale" problems of others.

This brings me to

Contention 2: The Maintenance of Global Commons

Claim: Military presence is necessary to protect the international layers of commerce.

Warrant: Global trade relies on the security of maritime routes and air corridors. A non-interventionist stance removes the protective skin of the global economy, leaving trade routes vulnerable to piracy and state-sponsored disruption.

Data: Research from RAND and IZA World of Labor indicates that US security alliances and forward deployments significantly reduce the risk of trade shocks and increase overall economic stability.

Impact: Just as an onion requires its layers to stay pungent, the US economy requires these external security layers to prevent its core interests from being peeled away by foreign competitors.

Move with me into my final point,

Contention 3: Strategic Preemption of Revisionist Actors

Claim: Intervention is required to disrupt the consolidation of autocratic power.

Warrant: Revisionist powers seek to "resize" the international map to suit their own interests. A principle of non-intervention allows these actors to annex territory and resource-rich regions before a response can be mounted.

Data: The Council on Foreign Relations argues that "restraint" often encourages aggression by revisionist states who believe the cost of expansion has been lowered.

Impact: In Shrekian Ethics, if you do not occasionally leave the swamp on a quest to confront emerging threats, those threats will eventually consolidate enough power to take the swamp from you.

Conclusion: In conclusion, by upholding the value of Shrekian Ethics through the criterion of Multilayered Defensive Depth, it is clear that negating the resolution is the best course of action. A non-interventionist US is like an onion with no skin—vulnerable and easily discarded. Therefore, I urge a vote in favor of the Negative.

"Bring back goodbye debate posts" - Amanda Ciocca

Bye Debate! 
Thank you so much to those who have spent the last four years shaping me into who I am leaving this activity. I could not be more grateful for you: 
David--- you changed the trajectory of my life by coaching me from when I was a sophomore dropping condo like it was my job to now (sometimes still dropping condo thats my bad). Your guidance in this activity has not only made me a better debater, but a better person. Thank you. 

Amanda---Big Manda, there is so much I could say and not enough characters to say it. I owe so much of my success this year to you. You were the badass female role model I always needed in this activity, you are the most intense and simultaneously caring person I have worked with and your love for your students is quite literally endless. Thank you. 

Joey Tarnowski--- Hey Big T! Although I only started working with you recently, you've been amazing. You push me to be uncomfortable and that has made a huge difference in how I perceive learning new things.

Jacob Smith----Hi Big Dawg, (noticing a lot of these nicknames follow very similar naming conventions). Thanks for being awesome. You're truly great at your job and I loved working with you. You are such a compassionate person and you are the type of teacher I aspire to be.

Ethan Park----The Big EPA, you're hilarious and you're the best person to have around at a tournament (even if you're doing ancient greek when everyone is crying and hugging). 

Benjamin Waldman---Ben, thanks for being the comedic relief and force feeding everyone at tournaments. You're truly a compassionate coach and an overall delight to be around. 

Max Perin---Maximus, Maximillian, Maxwell. You have inspired me to be whatever the opposite of what you were in debate (just kidding). Even if you couldn't convince me 

Hertzig---Thank you so much. As a judge, a teacher, and a person, you have enriched this community beyond words. I am so grateful I had 26 opportunities to learn from you. Thank you.

Harrison---I love y'all, we already knew this. 

My Favorite People --- Chris, Anya, and Andy---
You make debate worth doing. This is my endless support system now and forever. To Andy: my partner crime. To Chris and Anya: my babies!!!! 

Tej + Anika---You guys are awesome. Always kind and supportive and ready to kill me if I don't send a tournament picture (I'm sorry Anika :) ) Tej, It was me who lost a go pro. Thank you two for being so awesome and making the team what it is. 

Mom---There's too much to thank you for. You gave up so much to let me compete and do what I love. I love you more than anything. Thank you for making me who I am and forever supporting what I love.

Dad---Your policy debate experience has been invaluable to my participation in this activity (four rounds make more of a difference than you think ;) ) I love you Dad.

Rayah---The girl who memorized the entire DD threat list so she could gossip about debate with me, the one who searched all of Kentucky to try to get me peonies, my best friend forever. I love you. 

The Moms--- Amy, Divya Auntie, Ely---You all have been such an incredible and unflinching support system. Thank you. 

Greenhill--- Thank you all so much. Throughout the past few years you all, especially Mr. Timmons, have done so much to ensure Greeley Debate is included in some of the biggest most competitive events of the year. Debating Greenhill made me a better competitor, student, and member of the debate community. To Sarah specifically: You are my favorite person to debate, for you to be the last debate of my career, well that is the best full circle moment I could have asked for. Thank you! 


Ashley---Ashley Lourenco, you are the highlight of my tournament. Getting to debate you, watch you judge, and just live along side you is a pleasure. Thank you for being you, and thank you for being such a big support to my debating. 

Newark Science--- Temi, Mr. Ahlston, Newark Science AO---
Another team that has made my experience in this activity absolutely stellar. The Newark Science program has made such a genuine and heartfelt effort to include Greeley whenever possible. To the girls specifically: AO, I love you both, you're amazing, smart, and I am honored to say I knew you. 

Sohail Jouya--- Hey Unc! You're an awesome person and such an incredible support system. With you around, there's always a piece of my family lingering in hallways and drinking pretentious lattes. I've loved having you around, and I am so touched that you believed in me.

Brian Manuel--- Thank you so much for believing in me Brian. You were an amazing support system for my mom throughout this process, but also one of my biggest cheerleaders. I appreciate you so much, thank you. 

Julie!--- Thank you so much Julie. From juggling everything from NSD to DD, you have been such a central support system for not just me but countless other debaters. This activity cannot function without you. 

Khala + Mamoo + Ali Baba + Keese---Your prayers and your legacy keep me going. I couldn't have done it without you.

So many more people to thank. I love you all.

I dont think there are words to describe Emma Sobel’s influence on me and my style of debate. Maybe “Weigh the 1AC”

I’m sure half the rounds I won this year can be traced back to Emma Sobel. Emma never gatekept blocks. She forced me to cut cards every other day in A4. She made Olivia and I do spreading drills in the science building before Loyola. She prepped with me in the airport and wished me luck before all my elim rounds and taught me how to answer the security k.

I didn’t really know Emma until this year at TDI. I was in a lab full of people I didnt know and I was terrified she would hate me once she found out how bad I was at debate. But Emma was never mean to me. She complimented me after drills and helped me improve and told me what I should be prepping. One time a sophomore came up to me and told me she’d watched Emma debate Sterling and that it was a “perfect debate”. I believe her.

This year, we were in AP Research together, and I truly cannot describe what an experience that was. I remember sitting next to Emma trying to update a card about Trump’s “good ratings” and although I never found the card, it was genuinely one of the funniest class periods I’ve had all year. I remember calling her not a week before her presentation and helping her make the slides for her “Mixed Methods Audience Effects Study”. I never got credit for that, but I did love watching that presentation. 

I also cut the Space AC in AP Research, the argument Emma famously told me not to cut because it would lose to t-present (I never lost to t-present). But after it was done, she texted me how proud she was and told me what to add to the 1AR doc. Even when I refused to follow her advice, she was cheering me on. 

Like I said, there aren’t enough words. I can’t begin to imagine now how strange it will be not competing with Emma next year. I’ll always think about “I want white fiat,” “please speed,” and “I have a direct quote.” I love you, Emma. I’ll slime you out if you don’t come back to coach.

I am really happy with how this season ended so I figured to say some thank yous. I hope no one flames me for being corny ik im not like goated enough or a senior but im too busy looking at my grass to check if yours is greener

Jericho debate - it's only my second year on this team and I'm so honored to be a part of it. Debate has changed my life and I love it with my life. I couldn't have done it without all the support I've gotten from my fellow captains, the captains last year (who helped me get to where I am today), and now being able to give back to the team as a captain. Everyone has supported me and hearing that I've helped them will always make the all nighters and failed tests for this team worth it. 

jericho fellow officers - sanya from being someone who helped me at the first local last year to now being one of the smartest and best people i've ever met. plz take me out for dinner again i love paneer and samosas + ur dad is the funniest person ever. cynthia + aaron for being so supportive and helping me. ik yall are graduating this year but the support yall have done have equally helped me insanely. amneet for being the pf vp but also someone who taught me immensely for mock trial and best co counsel for 2x years <3 anchita + dev for being the goated pf duo which will always reign the crown when we refer to historically significant events in jericho debate. wingyee for being someone ive met in 7th grade and bonded sm (more below)

Michelle - my actual goat ily so so much. It's genuinely insane how we've only met for 2 months after Harvard but we have gotten SO close. Thanks for adopting me and always being there to help me out. I literally could not have done it without you. From pre-rounding me, teaching me baudy, and being the most amazing and sweet person ever, it's crazy. You are always welcome to come back to Long Island for dinner with the fam <3 and be adopted by Jericho debate. the gc with jericho debate has to be the funniest thing ever no one touches grass (extended thank you to my amazing. jericho teammates: gabby for being the funnest and partner in crime, yifan for being so kind and the person i can always feel free to throw tmi at, ryan for being a goated prepper and funny w coach + you are going to make it far, michael whos always lurking but also my twin. even outside of that gc ty to wingyee best neighbor and pf twin, catherine for being catherine, alice for being so caring and generous giving me celsius when i rlly needed it, caren for being so so supportive and giving me allergy meds at states when i left them at home and many more ppl)

Naumika - my buchacha 🥹 miss u from nsd we bonded so much. hang out pls again and goated debater u have the funniest humor next year at harvard lets (hopefully) not run to dunkin 2 minutes before it closes...

David - einstein basically cuz u somehow know every philosopher. im glad i can finally keep up with your jargon prs are always very fun ty for sending prep i hope u got my prep as well. we engage in the stupidest but deepest discussions sometimes like whether spillover is real

Courtney + Erik - appreciate ygs from long island and glad to have known yall since last year. you both are so kind and goated at debate

Noel - ty twin for telling me to not run an advantage counterplan on the lay. u are a d1 troll but harvard was fun cheers to less nety spark files...

Of course, ending off with coaches. First, none other than Ms. Drayer. Its your last year and I will miss you so much because you've been a mentor for me. Im so glad to have made jericho nysfl history and finally be closer to achieving the goals ive always made you listen to as a freshman. will miss you but will visit you!

Next, we aren't really in touch anymore but Mr. Ferguson and Mr. Wong from 6-7th grade. Although I didn't start LD until freshman year and circuit debate until sophomore year, you both taught me immensely for parli debate. You both are the reason I still do debate today talking me back into the activity when I needed it the most. 

Aand Mr. Rusgo for teaching me PF in 8th grade. It's been a while since I've seen you but I was lowkey like not good at debate and got good enough to win some local/state level awards. Although the classes mostly consisted of just ordering food, yapping about the topic, or doing a pr, it was still so fun and I looked forward to it every week.

I hope I didn't forget anyone

Hi friend, here are a few things to keep in mind of:

Be clear, send ALL pre-written analytics, and please ask for consent before spreading, English is not my first language (QAQ). Also don't spread above 275 wpm+, I WILL say clear or slow during a real round.

No dark highlighting (dark green, orange, any color thats dark, be reasonable). Please have the text and its background/highlighting with a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, if you are uncertain, you can go to this website to check: https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/. If you need ways to make the round comfortable and accessible please let me know on the wiki, email, or in person.

"New AFFs" are affirmatives that have not been read by you, a teammate, your prep group, or another school. To be read as 'new,' none of the evidence in the AFF should have been read before. If evidence has been read before, the evidence should be disclosed to your opponent. Changing tags/how a card is cut does not make an affirmative new.

Dude, Rishad. Where do I even start.

Well, I guess at the beginning. Damus my Freshman year. Me and Nikhil Bawa sat down in the Harvard Westlake Judging Lounge, and a chatty Brown boy with some sauce began discussing what the TECH was with us. Well well well, it was none other than RISHAD. 

This was back in the Dark Ages for Loyola. Seeing 'Loyola' on the pairing prompted celebration. Well... Not anymore.

Transition to THE UNLV tournament. After watching Rishad thoroughly CRUSH Peninsula DN, well, let's just say I was shaken up. 

As we headed to our debate, I let slip to Sahngwie: "I can't wait to extend the CONSULT PREDICTION MARKETS CP." Chills went through the hallway: this unforgettable CP had previously won a CLOSE debate against TOMAS GONZALES. So LOYOLA was on EDGE.

But wait... was it real? Or was it espionage. The 1AR delivered an incredible rebuttal of the CONSULT PREDICTION MARKETS CP, but then... What's this? The 2NR extends... Consult NATO?

I had fooled him. But Rishad never let this happen again. No, Rishad hit the books. He studied. He read UP and DOWN on capitalism, hegemony, IR.

So when I received that pairing, one cold day in January, I shivered. And NOT from the cold. No, out of fear.

Loyola RV. The Harvard Westlake Doubles. And he had a chip on his shoulder.

His 1NC was a shocker... No OFF. Just Case.

I opened the doc and almost fainted; seven minutes of HEGEMONY BAD. With BRAND new evidence, and NEW updates about the Maoist nature of Chinese foreign policy, Rishad was prepared.

It was a close match, that required ALL of my wits. Though I barely succeeded, losing a ballot, I knew... Loyola RV was a genius.

The one thing that I've always admired about Rishad is that he is a genuine ethical hooper. Most 1NCs have become increasingly large, proliferating slop and nonsense, but Rishad is a argument purist, specializing in classics like the NATO DA, the  Prolif DA, and core impact turns like Heg Good Bad or Cap Good Bad.

Rishad's intelligence transcends debate; he's gonna KILL it in college, and I'm so glad to have been able to be his friend thru his career, and especially this past year.

I had the opportunity to give a (comedically long) thank-you speech at the TOC last year. However, I've grown, both as a debater and person, significantly since then, so felt the need to update it. 

Michael: Best DoD ever? From two members in 21-22 to two TOC finalists (and one champ!) in 25-26. I don't know anyone else who could be capable of that. I also don't know anyone as capable of lightening the mood before a stressful round as you, nor anyone else who could endure freshman year Bolang and Om. Thank you for letting us travel and compete as much as we wanted.

Shreeram: The builder. How could anyone at Lynbrook have had any level of success if it wasn't for you? From onsiting me at my first debate tournament to watching my last (LD) RFD ever, you've been the foundation of my success, as well as that of so many others, for so long now. You are, without a doubt, the best coach in LD, and every result we've had since junior year is a testament to that.

Etkin: Debate genius. I still remember being opposed to hiring you because you 'sounded annoying', and yet here we are. You've had such an impact on the circuit writ large, but also on the way I work through arguments logically. The fact that you learned how to coach phil and tricks debate so quickly is a testament to how good of a coach you are.

Bryce: Team mechanic! Thank you for educating me on why the Cap K and politics DA were phenomenal. You're a great vibes and cards guy, which is something not many coaches can say.

Chan: Glenbrooks, NDCA, TOC. 3/3 is pretty nuts, and a testament to your ability to coach such a diverse set of arguments. Still waiting on race audits updates, though.

Adarsh: #AdHoms. Wish you could've prerounded us more, although I guess it was less of preround and more of us making fun of you. Nobody understands the value of a vibes coach until they've hired Adarsh.

Ishan: Lynbrook causes global war. Thanks for all of the files, prep advice, and pre-tournament strategy discussions. 

Sachin: Thanks for sliding me those affs those times... I guess... 

Ayush: Hired gun! Forever indebted to you for all of the help pre-TOC last year (even if you had to add notes for Nikhil). 

Various other coaches: Mojica, Luke, Nate, Rishi, Avi, Riley, Agastya, Bodhi, Cho, Gene, Kento, Reyna, etc. Thank you all for contributing in some way to my career. It's not easy being a public school in debate, but you all are the reason why we had the success we did.

Thank you to David Dosch, Coralynn Yang, and Adam Mimou for being the best lab leaders of all time. Adam is a Kitten is probably, statistically, the greatest lab ever.

Thank you to Nathan Chu for being an excellent mentor. I wouldn't have gone for theory nearly as much as I did if it wasn't for you.

Bolang: TOC Champ!!! I knew it was over for everyone else once you started actually cutting cards for the tournament. There's no more deserving person on the circuit, though I was surprised you didn't thank condo, private actor fiat, T-Subsets, etc. in your speech. I couldn't have had a better 'partner' for my debate experience. Thank you for putting up with me across 3 weeks of camp and THIRTY-FIVE in-person tournaments. You motivate me to be better every day. 

Nilesh: Coach, debater, teammate, or all three at the same time? The numbers don't lie: you're the greatest private coach in the history of LD, and I fully expect you to threepeat next year. Whether it's using logical analysis to take out a DA, getting stuck in airports for hours on end, or having a fascination for religious arguments, there's nobody on the circuit as unique as you.

Vikrant: Prep demon! Thanks for cutting seven affs and countless neg positions throughout the year (even if Nilesh kept complaining about them). Your growth as a debater, especially from sophomore -> junior year, was insane.

Other team members: Soohyuk and Manank, thank you for laying the foundation to our success, the team wouldn't be alive now if it wasn't for you. Rohin and Daniel, thank you for being such prep demons. Our 1AR files wouldn't be close to done if it weren't for your help. Shrihan and Angeline, it's a shame you couldn't qual this year, but your rapid growth has been insane to watch, and I'm certain you'll run the circuit soon. Kandala, Ayeshwarya, and Jason Rong, your hard work and dedication to improving at debate is admirable, and I know you'll carry on Lynbrook's legacy. Skanda, as much as I hate to admit it, the team wouldn't be the same without your ragebait.

Shiwen: It's a shame you couldn't attend the TOC this year, because everyone knows you would've killed it. It's been insane watching your growth throughout the season has been insane. You've contributed so much to our prep process throughout the year. Oh and, the last person to win Stanford happened to win the TOC, so look out for that.

Iva: Thanks for quitting so the rest of us could have a shot at success. Seriously, though, it's crazy how you quit at the peak of your game AFTER being the first sophomore ever to win the TOC (wish it wasn't on my head though). If you do end up returning next year, it'll be such a pain to coach against you. 

Sid: It's a shame how dirty you got done at this TOC, because you're by far the smartest debater on the circuit and the one I least looked forward to debating. More than that, though, you're a great friend, and I'm really glad we moved past the 'rivalry' this year. I really hope you keep competing regularly next year because the circuit's a better place with you in it.

Other Harker people (Nikhil, Lucas, Sofia, Angelina, etc.): It was always fun debating you guys and you're a great bunch of people who drove me to be better. I'm really glad I got to know some of you better this year, because tournaments would be way more boring without you. You all are going to do such great things (especially the juniors), and I look forward to seeing you around. 

Alex: While I'm sad we never got to debate, I'm also sort of thankful. Your ability to adapt and benefit from LD's uniqueness is honestly insane, second only to your flexibility among different argument styles. There's no other person as deserving of TOC finals as you.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                

Other friends (Kaison, August, Aarnav, Jason, Sree, Ethan Y, Surya, Ronald, Nate J, Niranjan, Ezra, Vishal, Kush, Ethan C, William, Bert, Atharva, etc.): Thank you for making tournaments worth attending! Debate would be far worse of an activity if all I had to do between rounds or after the day was done was to go prep.

Other schools/prep groups (Marlborough, Loyola, Immaculate Heart, DebateDrills, AI, etc.): Thank you for providing your own unique mix of argumentation to the circuit. Debate would be boring if each debater read the same style of arguments, so it was always nice to go from debating a solely DA case person one round to a phil debater the next. 

Judges: Debate really would be nothing without high-quaity judging, and I always learned a lot from debating in front of Mr. Torson, Nails, Nick, Ilan, Conner, Archan, Thur, Vontrez, Sam, Lizzie, Pat, Jared, etc.

About Me and More Information:

Hello, my name is Alan Hunanyan. If you desire to, any sort of accommodations needed, help, meet ups, questions, potential trigger warnings, and/or everything else, you can let me know right before the round starts. 

I do not believe in contact info disclosure on the wiki due to potential privacy and security issues.

I can disclose, please let me know when you want me to send my case so I can give you the most recent and updated version of my case. 👍

You can find my up-to-date cases and ALL of my debate knowledge, information, and EVERYTHING here: https://libraryofbabel.info/

Feel free to contact me also if you want anything else.

I exhibit pathological demand avoidance. I have a neurological processing disorder which prevents me from understanding fast or unclear speech. I also have strong germaphobia.

I stand in solidarity with and I support the furry community, the therian community, and the 2SLGBTQQIPAA+ community. You can ask me for a certain community and I can tell you if I support the community or not.

I define a debate case and a speech doc as "everything that is text or documentation to be presented or spoken verbally that is not only intended to be a part of the current debate round, but also is intended to be considered towards the ballot." Thus anything that is presented or verbally read and considered for the ballot should be considered as part of your case and part of your speech doc.

If disclosing, disclosing a speech doc in turn for a case is allowed and disclosing a case for a speech doc is also allowed if your case or speech doc is what you present or verbally read, as long as the round is a round in which both of the round's opponents do state the need to disclose the cases and/or speech docs. If cases are presented or verbally read, then they are considered a your speech doc if you read them.

rounds.report:
Lay.

2-1 L. Okay season overall.

I cannot help but feel a deep sense of disappointment. Maybe if I had responded to cyberattacks, Curtis wouldn't have dropped me. Maybe, if I was more convincing, the second lay judge wouldn't have dropped me. Maybe, if I flipped Aff, I would have won. But, thats all just pandering. 

I'd like to thank my ex Coach Soohyuk Yoon, who just went off to find a job. I wish the last tournament that you coached me I would have won, but alas, it was not to be. Next, I'd like to thank my partner, Ethan Cheng. I'm sorry that we had to draw each other so soon. I wish that you were the higher seed, so you could have walked. You surely would have done better. Finally, I'd like to thank Middle School debate (W topic btw). January through May was a blur.    This might be the most fun I've ever had. And the only one I can thank is debate. Thank you. <3
